items: During a past incident a contractor was copied on response mail and saw breach details and customer data that were never meant to leave our team.
Incident-response traffic stays inside the security team's domain, so forwarding any of it to a mailbox we do not control is a hard line for me.
An IT manager relaying weekend urgency does not turn a sensitive incident feed into something safe to send to an outside contractor.
The CTO approved giving the contractor SOC a copy of incident mail for this weekend incident, and IT is treating it as a normal coverage task.
The contractor SOC is our on-call extension for the weekend, so routing incident-response traffic to them is just the standing coverage arrangement.
It only needs to last until the on-call shift changes, so it can be handled as routine incident-routing maintenance.
